packages.title: Employee offboarding
packages.summary: A manager submits a leaver; access is revoked on the right day, equipment recovered, final pay scheduled, the exit interview held and the termination recorded.
packages.description:
Employee offboarding coordinates everything that has to happen when someone leaves. A manager or HR fills in the start form: employee number, last working day, reason, whether they are eligible for rehire and any notes.

The workflow reads the employee from your HR system (job, manager, privileged access, devices, leave balance) and evaluates the Offboarding controls decision table. Dismissals and leavers with privileged access lose access immediately; others on their last day. The table also decides whether an exit interview is offered and whether garden leave applies.

IT then revokes access and recovers equipment (the manager is emailed if anything is outstanding), payroll confirms the leave payout and final pay date, and HR runs the exit interview when required. The termination is recorded in the HR system, and the leaver and manager receive confirmation emails. Adapt the control rules to your security policy and the API paths to your HR system.

Assignees: pick the default IT owner, payroll officer and HR partner. Runs can pass it_owner_id, payroll_owner_id and hr_owner_id instead.
Edit the Offboarding controls rules to match your security and HR policy (revocation timing, exit interviews, garden leave).
Email: configure EMAIL_PROVIDER on the instance so the leaver and manager emails are delivered (the steps continue on error).

packages.summary: HR enters a new hire; the HR record, laptop, accounts, buddy and first-week plan are all arranged before day one, with a 30-day check-in.
packages.description:
Employee onboarding takes a new hire from signed offer to settled in. HR fills in the start form: name, personal email, job title, department, start date, manager, location and employment type.

The workflow creates the employee in your HR system, reads the department's laptop, systems, buddy team and welcome pack from the Onboarding checklist table, and evaluates the Onboarding track decision table to work out how many days IT needs and whether orientation applies. It then starts the IT setup sub-workflow, which gives IT a task due on the ready-by date and records the provisioning request in your IT service desk, while the hiring manager picks a buddy and writes the first-week plan.

When the manager is done, the new hire receives a welcome email with their work email, buddy, equipment and first-week plan. Thirty days later the manager gets a short check-in task. Adapt the checklist rows, the track rules and the two API paths to your systems.

packages.title: Equipment request
packages.summary: Employees request kit from an equipment catalogue; a cost and role policy routes approval, IT fulfils the request and the asset is registered.
packages.description:
Equipment request lets employees order standard kit (laptops, monitors, phones, headsets, chairs) from a themed form page. They start typing the item and pick it from the Equipment catalogue (its category, unit cost and lead time fill in), then add the quantity, the reason and when they need it. Submitting shows a confirmation screen and starts the workflow through its Form submitted trigger.

The workflow reads the item's category, unit cost, lead time and supplier SKU from the catalogue table, works out the total and evaluates the Equipment approval decision table. Low-cost accessories and executive standard kit are approved automatically; other requests go to the manager as a task with Approve and Reject buttons, and high-value items or furniture also need finance approval.

Once approved, the requester is emailed and IT gets a fulfilment task to order or pick the item and record the asset tag, serial number and delivery date. The asset is registered to the employee in your asset-management system and the requester is told it is ready. Adapt the catalogue rows, the approval thresholds and the asset API.

packages.title: Leave request
packages.summary: Employees request leave from a form; the balance, leave-type rules and an approval policy decide auto-approval, manager or HR review, then the leave is booked.
packages.description:
Leave request handles annual, sick, parental, bereavement and unpaid leave from one form. The employee enters the leave type, dates, number of working days and an optional reason.

The workflow reads the current balance from your HR system, looks up the leave type in the Leave types table (paid, certificate, notice, automatic limit) and works out the balance after the request and whether enough notice was given. The Leave approval decision table then approves short requests automatically, or sends them to the manager, and brings HR in for parental leave, unpaid leave or requests beyond the balance.

The manager can approve, decline or ask for a change; changed requests go back to the employee and are re-checked against the policy. Approved leave is booked in the HR system, added to the team calendar and confirmed by email. Adapt the leave types, notice periods and approval rules to your policy.

packages.title: Probation review
packages.summary: Every morning, employees whose probation ends within three weeks get a manager review; the outcome is confirmed, extended or ended and recorded.
packages.description:
Probation review makes sure no probation period ends without a decision. Every morning the scheduler asks your HR system for employees whose probation ends within the look-ahead window (21 days by default).

For each employee it starts the Probation review sub-workflow in the background. The manager gets a task due on the probation end date with a performance rating, a recommendation (confirm, extend or end) and development notes. The Probation outcome decision table turns that into the action, the HR status and any extension; a "confirm" with a below-expectations rating becomes a short extension.

The outcome is written back to the HR system, the people team is emailed the result and next step, and confirmed employees get a congratulations email. Adapt the look-ahead, the outcome rules and the API paths; your HR system should stop returning an employee once their review is recorded so they are not picked up twice.

packages.description:
Timesheet approval replaces emailed spreadsheets with one tidy form. Employees open the Weekly timesheet form page, pick the project from the Projects table (client and billable fill in by themselves), enter hours for Monday to Friday in a single row, describe the work, give a reason for any overtime and pick their approver as a Person. Submit shows a success screen.

The Form submitted trigger starts the workflow: it adds up the week, works out overtime above 40 hours and the billable value at the project rate, records everything in the Timesheets table and checks the week with the Timesheet checks decision table.

The approver gets a task with the hours laid out per day, the project budget used so far and Approve and Reject buttons with a comment. Weeks over 40 hours go on to an overtime check by payroll or a second manager. Approved hours are added to the project's hours, and the employee is emailed the decision with the comments. No integrations needed.

setup: Replace the sample rows in Projects with your projects: code, client, billable, hourly rate and hours budget. Untick Active for closed projects.
Share the Weekly timesheet form link (/f/<id>) with staff.
Adjust the Timesheet checks decision table if your overtime threshold is not 40 hours.
Optional: set EMAIL_PROVIDER so decisions are emailed (the console provider logs them).

packages.title: Training sign-off
packages.summary: Trainees submit course completion evidence on a form; their trainer signs it off or asks for more, and the training record and expiry date are kept.
packages.description:
Training sign-off turns course completions into a clear, auditable record. The Courses table is your catalogue: code, title, category, delivery, duration, the evidence the trainer expects and how many months the qualification stays valid. Sample courses include first aid, forklift operation, working at height, privacy and anti-bribery training.

A trainee opens the Training completion form page, looks up the course (its title, validity and expected evidence fill in), enters the completion date, hours and score, links the certificate or checklist, writes a short reflection and picks their trainer as a Person. Submitting shows a success screen and starts the workflow.

The workflow adds a row to the Training records table, works out the expiry date from the course validity and gives the trainer a sign-off task with Sign off and Needs more work buttons. Signing off records the assessment and expiry and emails the trainee; Needs more work sends the trainee a task to add evidence and resubmit, which goes back to the trainer. A seven-year retention policy is included for the records. No integrations needed.

Optional: apply the "Training records: 7 years" retention policy to the Training records table, and set EMAIL_PROVIDER so sign-off emails are delivered.

packages.summary: A Workday Hire event reads the worker, applies the job family checklist and onboarding plan, starts IT provisioning and has the hiring manager prepare day one.

packages.title: Workday time-off request sync
packages.summary: Every 30 minutes, time off requests from a Workday report sync to a Team calendar table; long or critical absences get a manager cover check.
packages.description:
Workday time-off request sync keeps a team calendar in UserTasks in step with Workday Absence Management. Every 30 minutes it calls a Workday report-as-a-service (RaaS) report that returns the time off requests updated in the last two hours, as JSON Report_Entry rows: worker, team, manager, type, dates, units, status and a critical-role flag.

Each request is matched to the Team calendar table by its request id: new requests are added and known ones updated with the latest dates and status, so cancellations and changes flow through. The Cover check decision table then decides whether the absence needs a cover check: critical roles, five or more days away and long-term leave do; cancelled, denied and short absences do not.

For each request that needs one, an async Confirm time off cover sub-workflow gives the manager a task form with Confirm cover and Flag a gap buttons, and the answer is written back to the calendar row. The sync itself completes in seconds; the cover checks wait for the managers.

packages.title: Workday worker change → access update
packages.summary: A Workday job change, org move or termination maps old and new jobs to access bundles, logs the request, and the manager approves or rejects it.
packages.description:
Workday worker change → access update keeps access in step with the job. When a Job Change, organization move or Termination completes in Workday, the event is posted to the workflow with the worker id and event id.

The workflow reads the worker and their staffing history from the Workday Staffing REST API, so it knows the job profile and supervisory organization before and after the change. The Access bundle mapping decision table turns each into a bundle code (terminations map to no access), and the Access bundles table says which applications and groups each bundle grants.

When the bundle changes, an access change request is logged and the manager gets a task form with the bundles to remove and add, a bundle lookup to correct it, a remove-by date and Approve / Reject buttons. The decision is written to the Access change requests table and posted as a comment on the Workday business process event. Provisioning in your identity system can then pick up the approved rows.

packages.title: Expense claims
packages.summary: Employees submit a claim from a form; category limits and an approval policy route it, and approved claims are queued for reimbursement.
packages.description:
Expense claims is a complete claim-to-reimbursement process. An employee fills in the start form (what the claim is for, the category, amount, date, receipt link and business purpose) from the Run dialog in UserTasks or from your own portal posting to the API.

The workflow looks the employee up in your finance system, reads the category rules from the Expense categories table (GL code, per-claim limit, receipt rule) and evaluates the Expense approval policy decision table. Small claims are approved automatically; everything else goes to an approver as a User Task with Approve, Reject and Send back buttons and the approved amount, GL code and cost centre pre-filled; the approver can recode the category from the same table.

The approver can approve, reject or send the claim back. Sent-back claims go to the claimant to fix and resubmit, then return to the same approval step. Approved claims are queued for reimbursement through the finance API and the claimant gets an email with the payment run date. A five-day SLA tracks the whole run.

Edit the Expense categories rows to your chart of accounts and limits, and the Expense approval policy rules to your delegation of authority.

packages.title: Invoice three-way match
packages.summary: Match each incoming invoice to its purchase order and goods receipts, pay matches within tolerance and route exceptions to accounts payable.
packages.description:
Invoice three-way match checks every vendor invoice against what was ordered and what was received before it is paid. Your AP or OCR capture system posts the invoice (number, vendor, PO number, total, currency and lines) to the workflow; there is no form to fill in.

The workflow reads the purchase order and the goods receipts from your ERP, works out the quantity variance (invoiced minus received) and the price variance against the received value, and evaluates the Match tolerance decision table with the vendor's risk rating. Exact matches and small variances are scheduled for payment on the due date from the vendor's payment terms, and the invoice is marked matched.

Anything else becomes a "Resolve match exception" task for accounts payable, with a two-day SLA, a reminder and escalation to the clerk's manager. AP can approve the variance and pay, put the invoice on hold and email the vendor for a credit note, or reject it. Adapt the tolerance rules, the ERP paths and the vendor emails to your process.

Assignee: pick the default AP clerk who resolves match exceptions (callers can pass ap_clerk_id per invoice).
Edit the Match tolerance decision table to your tolerance policy (percentage and absolute limits, vendor risk handling).
Inbound webhook: create a webhook for the workflow and point your AP / OCR system at it, or call the start API.

packages.title: Month-end close checklist
packages.summary: On the first of each month, open the close in the ERP and issue every checklist task with a deadline, evidence rule and an audit log.
packages.description:
Month-end close checklist runs your close from a table instead of a spreadsheet passed around by email. At 06:00 on the first of each month it works out the period to close (the previous month, unless you pass one), opens the close period in your ERP and reads every active row of the Close checklist table.

Each checklist row starts its own Close task run: the task is logged as open in the Close log, then assigned with a due date from its business-day deadline, a reminder and escalation to the assignee's manager. The person ticks Done and pastes the evidence link; where the checklist says evidence is required, the task comes back until a link is given. Blocked and not-applicable tasks are recorded with their notes. Every result is written to the Close log and back onto the checklist row.

The main run logs the close start, emails the finance team the list of tasks and completes, while the close tasks carry on in parallel. Edit the checklist rows, deadlines and owner roles to match your close calendar.

Edit the Close checklist rows: task, area, owner role, business-day deadline, system and whether evidence is required. Untick Active to skip a task.

packages.title: NetSuite vendor bill (AP) approval
packages.summary: NetSuite posts a vendor bill; subsidiary and amount limits pick the approvers, AP codes the cost centre and approves, rejects or holds, and NetSuite is updated.
packages.description:
NetSuite vendor bill (AP) approval runs bill approvals outside the NetSuite UI while keeping the approval status in NetSuite. When a vendor bill is created with approval status Pending Approval, a SuiteScript user event or a SuiteFlow action posts its internal id to the workflow.

The workflow reads the bill from the SuiteTalk REST record API with its item and expense sublists: vendor (entity), subsidiary, currency, total, tax, terms and due date. The AP approval limits decision table picks the approver level by subsidiary and amount and whether a financial controller or the CFO must also approve.

The AP approver sees the bill, its lines and the days to the due date, picks the cost centre from the Cost centres table (name, budget owner and NetSuite department fill in) and chooses Approve, Hold or Reject. Large bills go on to the second approver. The bill is then PATCHed in NetSuite: approvalStatus 2 (Approved) or 3 (Rejected), or kept at 1 with paymentHold set, with a memo, and AP is emailed the decision.

In NetSuite, turn on Accounting Preferences > Approval Routing > Vendor Bills so approvalStatus is used, and add a user event script (afterSubmit, create) or SuiteFlow action that posts {"bill_id": record.id, "tran_id": tranid} to the workflow webhook.
Assignees: pick the AP approver and the second approver (financial controller / CFO).
Replace the Cost centres rows with yours and set the AP approval limits per subsidiary (rules match on the subsidiary name).
Email: configure EMAIL_PROVIDER so AP gets the decision (the step continues on error).

packages.summary: A themed petty cash claim form with a cost-centre lookup and receipt link, float and limit rules, budget-holder approval and a ledger.
packages.description:
Petty cash claims takes the cash tin and the paper slips online. People fill in the Petty cash claim form: they find the cost centre in the Petty cash cost centres table (the budget holder and GL account fill in), pick the budget holder as approver, enter the amount, date and category and paste a link to the receipt. Its Submit claim button starts the Petty cash claim workflow with the form values as inputs and shows a success screen with the run reference.

The workflow reads the cost centre, adds up what was paid from its float this month in the Petty cash ledger and applies the Petty cash limits decision table: claims over NZD 250 or without a receipt over NZD 20 are declined with the reason, up to NZD 50 with a receipt is paid straight away, and the rest (or anything taking the cost centre over its float) goes to the budget holder.

The budget holder gets an Approve / Reject task with the receipt, the float used and the GL account, with a reminder and escalation. Every claim is in the ledger with its decision rule and payment date, and the claimant is emailed. Everything is built in.

packages.summary: Requesters submit a requisition; the purchasing policy sets approvals and quotes, and approved requests become a purchase order sent to the supplier.
packages.description:
Purchase requisition to PO takes a request from "I need this" to an issued purchase order. The requester fills in the start form: what they need, quantity, unit price, supplier, category, cost centre, the date they need it and a business justification.

The workflow totals the request, looks the supplier up in the Approved suppliers table (preferred status, payment terms, contract) and evaluates the Purchasing approval decision table, which sets the approver level and how many quotes procurement must collect. The manager approves or rejects with the cost centre and budget line. When quotes are needed, a buyer records up to three quotes and the selected supplier and amount.

The purchase order is then raised in your ERP with the supplier's terms and contract reference. The requester gets a confirmation and the supplier's orders address gets the PO. Edit the suppliers, the policy thresholds and the ERP request to match your purchasing rules.

packages.title: SAP purchase requisition → PO approval
packages.summary: An SAP S/4HANA purchase requisition is read over OData, routed by an approval matrix to approvers who pick the cost centre, then turned into a PO.
packages.description:
SAP purchase requisition → PO approval moves requisition approval out of SAP inboxes and into task forms people actually use. When a requisition is released for approval (a business event, a BTP Event Mesh message or a small ABAP job posting the number), the workflow reads it from the API_PURCHASEREQ_PROCESS_SRV OData service: the header and every item with material, material group, quantity, price, plant, purchasing organization and fixed supplier.

It totals the items and evaluates the PR approval matrix decision table on amount, material group and plant, which sets the approver level, whether finance must approve too and the SLA. The approver gets a task form with the items, a Cost centres lookup that fills the owner, remaining budget and G/L account, and Approve / Reject buttons; two-step rules add a finance approval.

Once approved, a purchase order is created with a deep insert into API_PURCHASEORDER_PROCESS_SRV A_PurchaseOrder, one PO item per requisition item with the approved cost centre, and the PO number is logged against the requisition.

CSRF: SAP OData POSTs need an x-csrf-token. Route calls through SAP API Management / BTP destination that fetches the token, or call through a gateway that handles it; the Create purchase order reference has an optional x-csrf-token header input if you fetch it yourself (GET with header x-csrf-token: Fetch).
Assignees: pick the default requisition approver and the finance approver (runs can pass approver_user_id and finance_user_id).

packages.title: SAP supplier invoice posting with 3-way match
packages.summary: A captured supplier invoice is matched to the SAP PO and goods receipts; variances outside tolerance go to AP, and matched invoices are posted to S/4HANA.
packages.description:
SAP supplier invoice posting with 3-way match takes invoices from your capture or OCR tool into SAP S/4HANA without blind posting. The capture tool posts the invoice header and line (supplier, invoice number, PO and item, quantity, unit price, gross amount) to the workflow.

The workflow reads the purchase order item from API_PURCHASEORDER_PROCESS_SRV and every goods receipt for it from API_MATERIAL_DOCUMENT_SRV (movement type 101), totals the received quantity and computes the quantity, unit price and amount variances. The Invoice tolerance decision table, modelled on SAP tolerance keys, decides whether the invoice is within tolerance.

Matched invoices are posted straight to A_SupplierInvoice with the PO and goods receipt reference, and the SAP invoice number and fiscal year are logged. Exceptions go to accounts payable on a task form showing PO, received and invoiced side by side, with a reason code lookup and Approve variance, Hold and Reject buttons; approved variances are posted with the chosen payment block.

CSRF: posting A_SupplierInvoice needs an x-csrf-token. Call SAP through API Management or a BTP destination that fetches it, or fetch it (GET with x-csrf-token: Fetch) and pass it to the optional x-csrf-token header input of Post supplier invoice.

packages.title: SAP vendor master change approval
packages.summary: A themed form requests a supplier bank change; SAP data is compared, finance reviews, the supplier is called back, treasury approves and SAP is updated.
packages.description:
SAP vendor master change approval protects one of the most attacked processes in accounts payable: changing where a supplier is paid. The requester fills in a themed start form with the supplier number, the new bank country, IBAN, SWIFT, account holder, effective date and the evidence reference.

The workflow reads the supplier, its company code data and its current bank details from SAP S/4HANA (API_BUSINESS_PARTNER: A_Supplier, A_SupplierCompany, A_BusinessPartnerBank), compares them with the request and evaluates the Bank change risk decision table: a different account holder or bank country is high risk and needs two call-backs.

Finance reviews the side-by-side comparison, an AP clerk calls the supplier on a number already on file and ticks off what was confirmed, and treasury gives the second, independent approval. Only then is the new bank detail created and the old one end-dated in SAP. Every step is written to the Vendor change audit log, and the requester is told when the change is live.

CSRF: the POST and PATCH to A_BusinessPartnerBank need an x-csrf-token. Call SAP through API Management or a BTP destination that fetches it, or fetch it yourself (GET with x-csrf-token: Fetch) and pass it to the optional x-csrf-token header input.

packages.title: Vendor onboarding with KYC
packages.summary: Screen new vendors for sanctions, registry and adverse media, tier the risk, review and verify bank details, then create the vendor in the ERP.
packages.description:
Vendor onboarding with KYC is a controlled path for adding a supplier. Procurement fills in the start form with the vendor's legal name, registration number, country, website, bank account, contact email, spend category and expected annual spend.

The workflow reads the country rating from the Country risk table and sends the company to your KYC screening service for sanctions, registry and adverse-media checks. The Vendor risk tier decision table turns the results and the expected spend into a tier (low, medium, high or blocked), the approvals needed and when to re-screen. Blocked vendors stop with an email to the requester. Medium and high risk vendors go to a compliance review, which can approve, approve with conditions or reject.

Every approved vendor then goes to finance to verify the bank account by calling a number from an independent source; the step repeats until the call-back is recorded. The vendor is created in the ERP with its tier and re-screen date, and the vendor contact gets a welcome email. Adapt the country ratings, the tier rules and the two API calls to your providers.

packages.summary: People request application access from a form; risk-based approvals route it, the grant is provisioned automatically and time-boxed access is revoked on expiry.
packages.description:
Access request and provisioning takes an application access request from a form through to a live grant. The requester picks the application, the role or entitlement, how long the access is needed (30 days, 90 days or permanent), who it is for and why.

The workflow looks the person up in the identity platform, reads the application from the Application catalogue (owner, risk level, privileged flag, provisioning group) and evaluates the Access approval path decision table. Every request goes to the line manager; medium-risk applications also need the application owner, and high-risk or privileged roles add a security review. Approvals run in sequence and any rejection stops the request and emails the requester.

Once approved, the grant is created through the identity API and the requester is emailed. For time-boxed access a sub-workflow waits 30 or 90 days and revokes the grant, so temporary access never outlives its approval. Adapt the catalogue, the approval rules and the identity API paths to your platform.

packages.title: Change management with CAB
packages.summary: An RFC form scores change risk, routes to pre-approval, CAB or emergency CAB, then tracks implementation and the post-implementation review in your ITSM.
packages.description:
Change management with CAB runs the change lifecycle from request to closure. The requester fills in an RFC: the system, change type (standard, normal or emergency), a description, the risk questions (customer impact, rollback tested, out of hours), the planned window and the backout plan.

The Change risk decision table turns those answers into a risk level and an approval path. Standard changes with little or no customer impact are pre-approved, emergencies go to the emergency CAB with a two-hour decision time and escalation, and everything else goes to the CAB. The change is registered in the ITSM straight away and an SLA tracks the window end. The CAB can approve, approve with conditions, reject, or defer to the next meeting, which brings the review back a week later.

Approved changes are marked scheduled and the requester is emailed. The implementer records the actual start and end and whether the change was implemented or rolled back, and the change manager completes the post-implementation review, which closes the change with a close code. Adapt the risk rules, the ITSM states and paths, and the people.

packages.title: Incident triage
packages.summary: Monitoring alerts open prioritised ITSM incidents automatically; repeat alerts are deduplicated and P1/P2 incidents page the on-call engineer with escalation.
packages.description:
Incident triage turns monitoring alerts into correctly prioritised incidents without anyone watching a dashboard. Your monitoring or alerting tool posts each alert (service, summary, severity, source, host and a dedupe key) to the workflow's webhook or start API.

The workflow looks the service up in the Service owners table for its tier, assignment group, on-call contact and runbook, and checks the ITSM for an open incident with the same dedupe key; repeat alerts are added to that incident as a work note. New alerts go through the Incident priority decision table (impact from the tier, urgency from the severity) to get P1 to P4 with response and resolution targets, an SLA is set and the incident is opened in the ITSM.

P1 and P2 incidents create an Acknowledge incident task for the on-call engineer with a 15-minute due time and escalation to the incident manager; acknowledging records the assessment and bridge link on the ticket and tells the business owner. P3 and P4 incidents are assigned to the team queue and the run completes. Adapt the service list, the priority matrix and the ITSM paths.

Edit the Service owners rows: every service your monitoring reports, its tier, assignment group, runbook and business owner email. Unknown services are treated as tier 3.
Review the Incident priority matrix and the response / resolution targets against your incident policy.
Webhook: create an inbound webhook for the Incident triage workflow and point your alerting tool at it, mapping its payload to service, summary, severity_hint, source, host and dedupe_key.

packages.summary: Staff borrow laptops, phones and headsets from a loan pool: manager approval, availability tracking, a return check with reminders and a full loan log.
packages.description:
IT equipment loans replaces the spreadsheet and the sticky notes on the IT desk. People open the Equipment loan request form, pick a device from the Loan pool table (only devices whose status is Available are offered), say when they need it and pick their manager. The serial number, type and pick-up location fill in by themselves.

The Form submitted trigger logs the request in the Loans table and gives the manager an approval task with Approve and Reject buttons, a reminder and escalation to their own manager after two days. On approval the device is checked again (someone else may have taken it), marked On loan, and the borrower is emailed where to collect it.

Each loan then starts a Return check sub-workflow: IT gets a check-in task due on the return date, with a reminder the day before. Checking it in records the condition and puts the device back in the pool (or into Repair when it is damaged); Extend moves the date and Not returned marks the loan overdue and chases the borrower. Everything is built in, so it works as soon as it is installed.

packages.title: Joiner, mover, leaver sync
packages.summary: A nightly job reads joiners, movers and leavers from the HR system and creates, updates or disables directory accounts with role-based groups, logging every action.
packages.description:
Joiner, mover, leaver sync keeps your directory in step with the HR system without tickets. Every night at 02:00 it asks the HR system for the workforce changes effective since the previous day.

Each change is processed in turn. The Role mappings table (department and job family) gives the birthright groups and licence for the role. Joiners get a new directory account with those groups, movers have their department, manager, groups and licence updated, and leavers are disabled with their sessions revoked and groups removed. Every action, including failures, is written to the JML sync log table with the HTTP status, so you can filter for anything that needs attention.

A summary of joiners, movers and leavers is written to the run log at the end. Adapt the role mappings to your groups and licences, and the HR and directory API paths to your platforms. Runs can also be started by hand with a since date to replay a period.

Directory integration: set the base URL of your directory or identity API and a token. The references expect POST /users, PATCH /users/{id} and POST /users/{id}/disable.
Edit the Role mappings rows: one per department and job family, with the comma-separated groups and the licence. Set default_groups and default_licence on the workflow for unmapped roles.

packages.title: Security alert enrichment
packages.summary: SIEM alerts are enriched with IP reputation, user and asset context, then auto-closed, opened as a SOAR case, or contained after analyst approval.
packages.description:
Security alert enrichment does the first ten minutes of triage for every SIEM alert. The SIEM posts the alert (id, rule name, source IP, username, hostname and severity) to the workflow's webhook or start API.

The workflow looks up the source IP in your threat-intelligence service, the user in the directory (department, privileged roles, MFA) and the host in the CMDB (criticality, owner, environment, EDR agent id). Lookups continue on error, so a missing user or unknown host does not stop triage. The Alert disposition decision table weighs the IP score, asset criticality, privileged user and severity and chooses auto-close, investigate or contain.

Benign alerts are closed in the SIEM with the enrichment as a comment. Alerts to investigate become a SOAR case with the observables attached, and the alert is linked to the case. Containment needs a person: the on-shift analyst approves host isolation within 30 minutes (escalating to the SOC lead), the EDR isolates the host and a case is opened either way. Adapt the disposition thresholds and the five API paths.

CMDB integration: base URL and token. Get asset expects GET /assets/{hostname} with criticality (low, medium, high, critical), owner and edr_host_id.
SIEM integration: base URL and token for PATCH /alerts/{id}. Security operations integration: base URL and token for POST /cases and POST /edr/hosts/{id}/isolate.
Assignees: pick the default SOC analyst who approves containment (alerts can pass analyst_user_id) and the SOC lead who receives escalations.
Review the Alert disposition thresholds, then create an inbound webhook for the workflow and point your SIEM alert action at it.

packages.title: ServiceNow change approval
packages.summary: ServiceNow sends a change for approval; CI criticality and a risk table route it, the CAB approves, rejects or asks for info, and the approval is written back.
packages.description:
ServiceNow change approval moves CAB decisions into a focused review task while ServiceNow stays the system of record. When a change request reaches Authorize, a business rule or flow posts its sys_id to the workflow.

The workflow reads the change from the Table API (type, risk, impact, CI, window, implementation / backout / test plans and conflicts), looks the CI up in the CI criticality table and evaluates the Change risk route decision table: emergency changes go to the ECAB, standard changes are approved automatically, high-risk changes and critical CIs go to the CAB and the rest to the change manager.

It finds the pending sysapproval_approver record for the change. The reviewer gets a task with the plans, the checks for the route and Approve, Request info and Reject buttons. Approve and Reject PATCH the approval record with the comments, so the ServiceNow change model moves on by itself; Request info adds a work note to the change. The change team is emailed the decision.

For candidates the incident manager gets a 30-minute review task with Declare major incident and Not a major incident buttons, the proposed severity and cadence filled in. The decision is written back to the incident as a work note with its major incident state, and a declared major incident emails the service's stakeholders with the impact, the incident manager and the next update time.

packages.title: Complaint handling with SLAs
packages.summary: Agents log a complaint; the customer tier and an SLA matrix set response and resolution targets, with escalation, compensation approval and CRM case resolution.
packages.description:
Complaint handling with SLAs gives every complaint a clear target and an owner. A service agent logs the complaint from a form: customer email, order number, category, severity, description and channel.

The workflow finds the customer in your CRM (tier and lifetime value) and evaluates the Complaint SLA matrix decision table, which sets the first-response hours, resolution days, handler level and how much compensation a handler can offer. It opens a case in the CRM, starts a resolution SLA and sends the customer an acknowledgement with the case number and response target.

The handler investigates in a User Task due on the resolution date, with reminders and escalation to a supervisor if it sits untouched. They record the root cause, resolution and compensation. Compensation over the handler's limit (or a "needs supervisor" outcome) goes to a supervisor, who can approve or send it back. The case is resolved in the CRM and the customer receives the resolution email. Adapt the matrix, limits and CRM paths.

packages.summary: Account managers register a new business customer; KYC screening, a credit report and a risk rating set the tier and limit before the account is opened.
packages.description:
Customer onboarding with KYC takes a new business customer from the sales hand-off to an open account. The account manager fills in the form: company name, registration number, country, primary contact, product and expected monthly volume.

The workflow reads the country risk from the Country risk table, runs registry, sanctions and PEP screening through your KYC provider and pulls a commercial credit report. The Customer risk rating decision table combines the KYC result, credit score, country risk and volume into a risk tier, credit limit and payment terms, and decides whether compliance must review the customer. Clean, low-risk customers go straight through.

Compliance can approve (adjusting the tier, limit and terms), request documents from the account manager, which loops back to the same review, or decline. Approved customers get an account in billing and CRM with the agreed limit, a welcome email goes to the primary contact, and the onboarding manager gets a kickoff task. packages.summary: Enrich each inbound lead, score it with a routing table, create it in the CRM with its territory owner, and alert sales or start nurture.
packages.description:
Lead routing and enrichment handles every inbound lead the moment it arrives. Your website or forms tool posts the lead (email, name, company, country, company size, source and message) to the workflow; nobody has to triage a shared inbox.

The Lead score & routing decision table turns company size, industry, region and source into a segment, a score and a priority.

The lead is created in the CRM with its owner and score. Sales-ready leads (score 60 or more by default) are emailed to the owner with the context they need for first contact; the rest are added to the territory's nurture list in your marketing platform. packages.title: Quote approval with discount tiers
packages.summary: Sales reps submit a quote; a discount authority table sets who approves, and each approver can approve, reject or counter before the CPQ is updated.
packages.description:
Quote approval with discount tiers enforces your discount authority without chasing approvals over chat. The sales rep fills in the start form: quote id, customer, product, annual list price, discount, term, payment terms and a justification.

The workflow works out the net annual price and the deal value over the term, then evaluates the Discount authority decision table. Up to 10% is approved automatically; above that the sales manager approves, above 20% the VP sales as well, and above 30% (or on very large deals) the deal desk and the CFO join. Approvals run in sequence, each with a one-day due date, a reminder and escalation, and each approver can approve (adjusting the approved discount), reject or make a counter-offer.

The final decision is written to the quote in your CPQ system and the rep gets an email: approved with the discount and conditions, rejected with the reason, or the counter-offer to take back to the customer. Adapt the thresholds, the approver chain and the CPQ call to your sales policy.

packages.summary: A Salesforce Flow submits an opportunity discount; tiers decide the approvers, the sales manager then finance approve, and the status goes back to Salesforce.
packages.description:
Salesforce opportunity discount approval gives your deal desk a clear, tiered approval without building approval processes in Salesforce. When a rep sets a discount and submits it, a record-triggered Flow (or a platform event subscriber) posts the Opportunity Id and the owner's email to the workflow.

The workflow reads the opportunity over the REST API (amount, stage, close date, term and the Discount_Percent__c / Discount_Approval_Status__c custom fields) and runs a SOQL query for its OpportunityLineItem records to see every product's list price, sales price and line discount. The Discount tiers decision table decides whether the discount is within the rep's authority, needs the sales manager or needs the sales manager and finance.

The sales manager's task has a Justification lookup from the Discount reason codes table, which fills in the normal ceiling and the evidence expected, and Approve / Reject buttons. Finance then confirms the approved discount for Tier 2 and Tier 3. The decision is written to the opportunity with PATCH (status, approved discount and notes) and the owner is emailed.

packages.summary: Monthly SOC 2 / ISO 27001 evidence run: automated controls are pulled from your systems, owners of manual controls are asked for a link, all logged for the auditor.
packages.description:
Audit evidence collection keeps your evidence folder current without a scramble before the audit. Each month it reads the Controls data table (framework, reference, evidence type, owner, frequency) and works through the controls that are due: monthly controls every month, quarterly ones in January, April, July and October.

Manual controls get a "requested" row and a Provide audit evidence run, in which the control owner submits a link or marks the control not applicable, which the compliance lead must accept. Reminders and escalation keep requests moving. At the end the compliance lead gets a summary with the counts.

packages.title: GDPR data subject requests
packages.summary: Handle access, erasure and other privacy requests: statutory deadline, identity check, search of CRM, billing and support, erasure, and a DPO-approved reply.
packages.description:
GDPR data subject requests takes a privacy request from receipt to response inside the statutory deadline. The privacy team (or your web form posting to the API) fills in the start form: who is asking, their email, the request type (access, erasure, rectification, portability, objection), the jurisdiction and the date it arrived.

The Statutory deadlines decision table sets the response deadline and whether it can be extended (one month under EU and UK GDPR, 45 days under CCPA, 15 days for a CCPA opt-out) and the run gets an SLA to match. The request is added to the DSAR register and nothing is searched until the privacy team has verified the requester's identity; they can ask for more information or reject the request. Once verified, the CRM, billing system and support desk are searched by email, and for erasure requests an erasure is requested in each system, with any records kept by law listed.

The DPO reviews a drafted response with everything found, edits and approves it or sends it back, and the approved response is emailed to the requester and the register row closed. Adapt the deadline rules to your legal advice and the three system references to the systems that hold personal data.

packages.summary: Anyone raises a risk on a form; a 5×5 matrix rates it, the owner accepts, mitigates or escalates within an SLA, and a weekly job re-reviews due risks.
packages.description:
Risk register gives you a living register instead of a spreadsheet nobody opens. The Risks table holds each risk with its category, department, likelihood, impact, score, rating, owner, controls, response, mitigation plan, residual score and next review date. Six sample risks are included so the register is not empty on day one.

Anyone can raise a risk on the Raise a risk form page: a title, category, description, likelihood and impact (1-5 with plain-language labels), existing controls and the risk owner as a Person. The Risk submission workflow scores it (likelihood × impact), rates it with the Risk rating decision table (Low, Medium, High, Extreme), sets an SLA for the owner's review by rating and adds it to the register.

The owner reviews it in a task form with Accept, Mitigate and Escalate buttons: a mitigation plan, target date and residual rating are recorded, an escalation emails the risk committee, and the task escalates to the owner's manager if it sits for three days. A second workflow, Weekly risk review, runs every Monday: every open risk whose review date has passed goes back to its owner through a sub-workflow (still valid, rating changed, close risk). No integrations needed.

packages.title: Supplier risk review
packages.summary: Adding a supplier or flagging it for review pulls a fresh risk rating, sets the tier and next review date, and sends high-risk suppliers to procurement.
packages.description:
Supplier risk review keeps your supplier register's risk ratings current. It runs whenever a row in the Suppliers data table is created, or updated with "Review requested" ticked, and fetches the supplier's financial score, cyber score, ESG flags and sanctions screening from your risk-intelligence provider.

The Supplier risk decision table combines those scores with the supplier's criticality and annual spend into a risk tier, a review cadence and a recommended action. The workflow writes the tier, scores and next review date back to the row and clears "Review requested", so its own update does not start another review. High and critical suppliers go to procurement as a User Task to accept the risk, agree a mitigation plan or plan an exit, with a five-day SLA; the business owner is told when the supplier is flagged and when it is decided.

Adapt the Supplier risk rules to your risk appetite, the reference to your provider's API, and the Suppliers columns to your register.

packages.title: AI ticket triage with human review
packages.summary: An AI agent classifies each helpdesk ticket and drafts a reply; confident, low-risk answers go out automatically and the rest wait for a person.
packages.description:
AI ticket triage with human review puts an AI agent in front of your support queue without letting it answer everything on its own. Your helpdesk posts each new ticket (id, subject, body, customer email, channel and plan tier) to the workflow.

The Ticket triage agent returns the category, urgency, sentiment, a short summary, a suggested reply and its confidence. The Triage routing decision table then decides: confident how-to and low-urgency answers are posted automatically; security issues, critical tickets, enterprise billing and anything the agent is unsure about go to a person, with a queue and priority set either way.

The "Review AI triage" task shows the ticket, the summary and the draft reply. The reviewer corrects the category and priority, edits the reply and sends it, escalates the ticket (which moves it to the escalation queue and emails your support leads) or discards the draft and leaves the ticket for an agent. Every ticket is tagged so you can measure how often the AI reply was used. Adapt the agent instructions, the routing rules and the helpdesk calls to your tooling.

Assignee: pick the default support reviewer (runs can pass reviewer_id, e.g. per queue).
Tune the Triage routing rules: which categories and confidence levels may be answered automatically. Start strict and loosen as you review results.
Inbound webhook: create a webhook for the workflow and point your helpdesk's new-ticket trigger at it.
Email (optional): configure EMAIL_PROVIDER and set escalation_email for the escalation notice (the step continues on error).

packages.title: Document generation pipeline
packages.summary: Turn contract data from any app into a filled Word contract and Excel fee schedule, file both in your DMS and send the contract for e-signature.
packages.description:
Document generation pipeline produces contract documents without anyone opening Word. An application (your CRM, billing system or a back-office tool) posts the contract data: document type, customer, reference, start date, amount, term, signer and the URL of the Word template.

The Document templates table sets the title, file name pattern, DMS folder, retention period, body text and whether the document type needs a signature. The workflow fills the Word template's {{TITLE}}, {{CUSTOMER}}, {{DATE}}, {{AMOUNT}}, {{REFERENCE}} and {{BODY}} placeholders and, when an Excel template URL is passed, fills a fee schedule with the dates, total and monthly equivalent.

Both files are registered in your document management system with their metadata and retention. Document types that need a signature are sent to the signer through your e-signature service, and the signer gets an email with the signing link. Add rows for your own document types and point the two integrations at your DMS and e-signature provider.

Document management system: set the base URL and API token. Register document posts the generated file URL and metadata to /documents.
E-signature service: set the base URL and API token. Create signature request posts to /signature-requests.
Edit the Document templates rows: titles, file name patterns, folders, retention days, body text and which types need a signature.
Email (optional): configure EMAIL_PROVIDER so signers get the signing email (the step continues on error).

packages.title: Event-driven ETL
packages.summary: Each new row in an Orders staging table is normalised, converted to the base currency, loaded into the warehouse and marked loaded or failed.
packages.description:
Event-driven ETL loads orders into your data warehouse the moment they are staged. Anything that writes a row into the Orders staging table (a CSV import, a form, another workflow or the API) starts a run for that row.

The workflow normalises the row: an upper-case currency code, a lower-case email, a trimmed customer name and an ISO order date. It looks up the exchange rate in the Currency rates table, converts the amount into the base currency, builds the warehouse record and posts it to the warehouse ingest API.

The staging row is then updated with load_status loaded (and the warehouse id) or failed (with the reason: no rate, or the HTTP status). The trigger listens to created events only, so these updates do not start new runs. Adapt the record fields to your warehouse schema and keep the rates current.

packages.title: Order orchestration API
packages.summary: A synchronous order endpoint for your storefront: validate, price, fraud-screen, reserve stock, authorise payment and create the shipment in one call.
packages.description:
Order orchestration API turns one storefront call into a complete, ordered set of back-office steps. The storefront posts the order (order id, customer, email, lines with sku, quantity and price, the shipping address and a payment token reference from your payment provider) and waits for the answer: the workflow runs as middleware and its response is the result.

The workflow rejects incomplete orders straight away, then totals the lines and adds shipping and tax. The Fraud screening decision table looks at the order value, shipping country, whether the customer is new and whether billing and shipping countries differ, and returns accept, review or reject with a risk score. Accepted orders reserve stock in the inventory API, authorise the payment and create the shipment in the fulfilment API. If the payment is declined the reservation is released.

Orders flagged for review are still accepted, but the shipment is created on hold and a Manual fraud review runs in the background: a reviewer releases the shipment or cancels the order, voiding the authorisation and releasing the stock. The caller always gets result, order_status, reason, reservation_id, authorization_id, shipment_id and estimated_delivery. Card data never passes through the workflow.

packages.title: Scheduled data reconciliation
packages.summary: Every morning, yesterday's orders are matched to billing invoices; missing invoices and amount mismatches are recorded and a summary is sent.
packages.description:
Scheduled data reconciliation checks that every order was billed correctly. Each morning at 05:30 it reads yesterday's orders from your order system and the invoices for the same date from your billing API (or any date you pass as as_of).

For each order it finds the invoice with the same order id and classifies the pair: matched, missing invoice, or amount mismatch (a difference larger than the tolerance). Exceptions are inserted into the Reconciliation exceptions table with the amounts and difference, ready for finance to work through.

At the end it counts the results, emails a summary to finance operations and posts the same totals to an ops webhook. Adapt the two list endpoints, the matching key and the tolerance; nothing in the run needs a person.

packages.title: Webhook multi-system sync
packages.summary: A CRM "account updated" webhook is validated and fanned out to the ERP, billing platform and support desk, with every result written to a sync log.
packages.description:
Webhook multi-system sync keeps customer master data consistent across systems without anyone touching it. Your CRM posts an "account updated" webhook with the account id, name, billing address, tax id, status, owner and change time.

The workflow rejects payloads without an account id or name, then builds a payload per target system and calls them one after another: PUT the customer into the ERP, POST a sync to the billing platform and PATCH the organisation in the support desk. An HTTP error from one system does not stop the others: each call is checked for a status of 400 or above and logged as a failure or a success in the Sync log table.

Adapt the three payloads to your systems' field names, point the integrations at your APIs and create an inbound webhook for the workflow in your CRM. The Sync log gives you a monitoring view and the rows you need to replay a failed sync.
